general.temas: The head-to-head debate between Sánchez and Feijóo dominates the front pages, with assessments of the result, the candidates’ strategies and the electoral repercussions. Ayuso’s visit to Ceuta, Morocco’s temporary halt to construction work there and Alcaraz’s victory also feature repeatedly. Only Público highlights the Justice Ministry’s appeal to avoid releasing the records of Franco’s exhumation.
general.motivo_crispacion: The election campaign is generating considerable tension, particularly over Feijóo’s attacks on Sánchez and the recriminations over corruption, immigration and other issues during the debate. Disagreements over the result and criticism of Sánchez’s performance are prolonging the confrontation between parties and within the left. The interruption of construction work in Ceuta adds tension between Spain and Morocco. Sports, cultural and service news partly offset that atmosphere.

El País.resumen:
- The gap between the PP and PSOE is narrowing in the 40dB. poll, which also records a drop in support for Vox.
- The poll and the analysts consulted name Feijóo the winner of the debate against Sánchez.
- Several articles examine the candidates’ strategies and Sánchez’s alleged passivity.
- Journalists and experts examine controversial claims, lies and half-truths from the head-to-head debate.
- The front page also covers the reaction on social media and an anecdote about the moderator.
El País.motivo_populismo: An analytical tone predominates, although expressions such as “goes on the attack,” “duel” and “lies and half-truths” heighten the sense of confrontation.
El País.sesgo: The selection focuses on the dynamics of the debate and electoral strategy, particularly Sánchez’s alleged passivity. At the same time, it highlights Feijóo’s victory both in the poll and in the analysts’ assessments.

El Mundo.resumen:
- The Supreme Court demands compliance with the order to withdraw voting rights from 163,355 people who acquired Spanish citizenship under the grandchildren’s law, with 901 exceptions.
- The front page highlights Feijóo’s victory in the debate according to a poll, criticism of Sánchez and La Moncloa’s defence of his strategy.
- It also covers statements by Abascal and Ayuso about Sánchez and the electoral contest.
- The government approves the decree on data centres despite objections from the employers’ association; the PP promises to repeal it.
- Morocco temporarily blocks construction work in Ceuta, two Russian missiles land in Poland and stock markets register sharp falls.
El Mundo.motivo_populismo: Expressions such as “the man who finished off Pedro Sánchez,” “the same old bad guys” and “fateful week” add drama and disparagement, although other headlines maintain an informative tone.
El Mundo.sesgo: The selection and wording show an approach critical of Sánchez and highlight Feijóo’s advantage in the debate. La Moncloa’s defence of Sánchez’s strategy is also included.

ABC.resumen:
- The EU and the UK agree on a rapprochement to begin reversing Brexit.
- Police thwart the establishment in Spain of a cell of the cyberterrorist organisation NoName057(16).
- Vivas praises Ayuso in contrast to Sánchez, and the bishops rule out issuing their own statement to guide voters in the election.
- An incident involving the Moroccan navy brings construction work in Ceuta to a halt for hours; the Castellana Norte tunnel will open in December.
- In sports, the women’s national team squad announcement and Alcaraz’s victory stand out; political and cultural opinion columns are also included.
ABC.motivo_populismo: Informative headlines predominate, but emotive or disparaging expressions such as “destroys,” “spat” and, in one column, “massacre” and “cheerleaders” also appear.
ABC.sesgo: An approach critical of Sánchez and favourable to PP figures can be seen in the selection of a news story about Vivas’s praise for Ayuso and a column disparaging “pro-Sánchez media figures.” The latter is an opinion piece and does not by itself represent the entire front page.

Público.resumen:
- The front page focuses on the debate between Sánchez and Feijóo, with several stories about their accusations and the repercussions.
- La Moncloa rejects the claim that Feijóo won the debate; Colau criticises Sánchez’s stance towards the right.
- The head-to-head debate drew a total of 10 million viewers and generated memes.
- Other headlines address deaths in care homes and Ayuso’s explanation of her purchase of a penthouse.
- The Justice Ministry appeals to avoid releasing the records of Franco’s exhumation, whose public interest is asserted in another story.
Público.motivo_populismo: Expressions such as “the economics of Feijóo’s falsehoods” and “the devastating video,” together with the jibe that “even his own side are in fits of laughter,” lend a disparaging and sensationalist tone, although there is no apparent explicit appeal to the people against the elites.
Público.sesgo: The selection and wording present an approach that is particularly critical of Feijóo and Ayuso, while describing Sánchez as moderate. They also include criticism of Sánchez and the Justice Ministry.

OKdiario.resumen:
- The election campaign dominates the front page, with the head-to-head debate between Feijóo and Sánchez and comments by Juan del Val about the PSOE.
- Feijóo visits El Hierro and Ayuso calls for voters in Ceuta to unite behind the PP.
- Alcaraz beats Cobolli and reaches the semi-finals of the ATP Finals unbeaten.
- A study proposes a date for the fall of Babylon; a reflection by Ortega y Gasset is also included.
- The front page includes beauty and food content and padel deals.
OKdiario.motivo_populismo: Alarmist expressions such as “they invade you” and “it would be extremely serious” stand out, alongside sensationalist phrases such as “a steamroller,” “a thrashing” and “out-of-this-world bargains.”
OKdiario.sesgo: The political selection and wording give prominence to the PP and present Feijóo’s victory in the debate as fact, alongside a critical assessment of the PSOE. These headlines do not include equivalent favourable assessments of the PSOE.

opiniones.comunista:
I am less interested in who won the head-to-head debate than in who wins when politics becomes a contest of gestures. Amid polls, silences and recriminations, housing came up in the debate; the crucial question is whether it will be defended as a right or left to the discretion of those who profit from it.

The decree on data centres raises another class dispute. The employers’ association warns of a risk to investment and the PP promises to repeal the measure. I believe the public interest cannot be measured by the expectations of big capital: economic activity must be subject to democratic control and serve the working majority. We need strong public services and collective ownership in strategic sectors, not a democracy limited to choosing administrators of private interests.
opiniones.anarquista:
I see the election debate is once again being presented as a duel of winners and losers. But choosing who will wield power is not the same as deciding collectively about our lives. I distrust both the parties that aspire to govern and the idea that freedom can be delegated every few years.

The order to exclude thousands of people who have acquired citizenship from voting also shows how far rights depend on decisions made from above. I am not content simply to demand a ballot for more people: I want a society where no one needs permission from an authority to participate in decisions that affect them.

Against politics as spectacle, I stand for organising in neighbourhoods and workplaces, self-management and mutual aid. Individual freedom needs a free community, without hierarchies that turn some people into leaders and others into spectators.
opiniones.liberal:
The election debate leaves a more important question than who won the head-to-head: how much room do the candidates want to leave for citizens’ freedom? I am not looking for a government that directs every decision, but a limited one that protects rights, guarantees legal certainty and is accountable.

The approval of the decree on data centres therefore deserves rigorous scrutiny. The employers’ association warns of risks to investment; I would not take that figure as an established fact, but I would take it as a reason to demand that the costs of the measure be justified. Innovation needs clear rules, not unnecessary obstacles. It also needs low taxes that allow families and businesses to decide what to do with more of their money. Economic freedom does not eliminate personal responsibility: it demands it.
opiniones.extrema_derecha:
It is not enough for me that Feijóo won the debate according to the polls. A country does not regain control of its destiny with a victory on television. I want concrete commitments: guarded borders, immigration subject to strict rules and the ability to expel those who have no right to remain in Spain, with the appropriate legal safeguards.

What happened in Ceuta calls for firmness and clarity. If there is a dispute over the location of the construction work, it must be clarified; but Spain cannot give up defending its sovereignty or protecting its borders to avoid diplomatic discomfort.

I also expect the Supreme Court’s ruling on the electoral roll to be enforced. The right to vote is too important to be treated as just another campaign issue. While the political and media elites count gestures and silences, I prefer to ask which programme guarantees security, the continuity of our traditions and equality before the law.
opiniones.centro:
I am concerned that the election debate is being judged almost exclusively by who won the duel. According to the 40dB poll, more viewers gave victory to Feijóo than to Sánchez; that is a result worth acknowledging. But moderation does not mean remaining silent in the face of accusations: it requires responding with verifiable arguments and explaining one’s own decisions.

I am also troubled by the Supreme Court’s order on voting by people who acquired citizenship under the grandchildren’s law. Court rulings must be obeyed, and the authorities must explain clearly how the order will be applied and ensure that those who are entitled to vote can exercise that right.

As for the decree on data centres, we need rules that provide certainty for investment and protect the public interest. I would prefer an open review with the sector and a broad agreement to a promise simply to repeal it: lasting reforms require dialogue, not abrupt reversals.
